title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 7-9): in the 1986 'Ateliers' notes Grothendieck is building an axiomatic, combinatorial formalism of 'figures'. An 'atelier' A is a set of figures equipped with relations written ◁ (or a related relation), ≪ and a support map | |. The model case is A = Figurations(E), the figures in a space E. On p. 7 he poses a universal problem. Given a 'nullité' N ⊂ A, a class of figures to be declared null, he wants a morphism p : A → A/N that kills N (or some class containing N). It should be universal: every morphism of ateliers f : A → A' killing a class ⊃ N factors uniquely through p.

He makes the morphisms precise as pointed set-maps f^ : A ⊔ {p} → A' ⊔ {p} sending the base point to the base point and compatible with ◁, ≪ and | | on Â. This is like maps of pointed sets, or partial maps where figures sent to the base point are 'killed'. The type example is A = Figurations(E) with N = {X ∈ A : |X| ⊂ E∖E'}, for which A/N should be Figurations(E'), suitably read as a quotient of A∖N. Modern analogues are restricting or quotienting a stratified or combinatorial model by the part supported off E', the collapse X/Y of a CW pair, and passing to the complement of a sieve or ideal in a poset.

Page 8 is a short meta-mathematical assessment.
- He doubts that such a construction exists in general: it 'announces itself as a bit delicate'.
- Test case 1° is a set-theoretic ('ensembliste') atelier. He says even this is not evident, especially without a 'modéré/modérateur'-type hypothesis on the atelier. This holds even for very special N, such as Omb° F (an 'open shadow' of a figure F, apparently) or Supp F.
- Test case 2° is a 'maquette' A with N an arbitrary subset, where the relevant order is discrete (NB x ≤ y ⇒ x = y). Here the quotient should simply be the maquette A∖N, which is 'pas sorcier'. With a trivial order there are no compatibility constraints, so deleting N and sending it to the base point is clearly universal.
- Finally he notes that the link with the formalism of 'segments' (reading uncertain) could be modelled on 'CF VIII p. 70 ff', an internal cross-reference to earlier notes, probably chapter VIII. He says he lacks the energy ('pas la pêche') and drops it for now.

Page 9 then moves on to subdivisions. So the quotient-by-nullité problem is left open on this page.
errors: No mathematical errors. The only claim made, that for a maquette with discrete order the quotient by an arbitrary subset N is A∖N, is essentially trivial and correct under the pointed-map description of morphisms. The general existence question is explicitly left open, not answered.

ideas.what: Universal quotient A → A/N of a combinatorial 'atelier' of figures by a class N of null figures, with morphisms as base-point-preserving maps A ⊔ {pt} → A' ⊔ {pt}
ideas.modern_name: Quotient/cofibre of a pointed combinatorial structure; collapse X/Y; restriction of a stratified space to the complement of a closed union of strata; localization of a poset at the complement of an ideal
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard folklore (CW/simplicial collapse; quotients in pointed categories); no specific attribution for 'ateliers'
ideas.where_published: Ateliers notes unpublished; the theme of tame/combinatorial topology appears in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), but not this formalism

ideas.what: Test case: maquette with discrete order, quotient by arbitrary N is A∖N
ideas.modern_name: Deleting a subset of a discrete poset / pointed set quotient

ideas.what: Test case: set-theoretic atelier with N = Omb° F or Supp F, existence of quotient doubtful without a tameness ('modéré') hypothesis
ideas.modern_name: Existence of quotients in categories of stratified/tame spaces requires finiteness or tameness hypotheses (cf. o-minimal quotients, van den Dries)
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimal geometry (van den Dries, 1980s-90s) for definable quotients
ideas.where_published: Tameness hypotheses appear in spirit in Esquisse d'un programme §5-6

missed.claim: The existence and construction of a universal quotient A/N of an atelier by a nullité N is posed and abandoned. Even the set-theoretic case with N = Omb° F or Supp F is flagged as non-evident, and the link with the 'segments' formalism is postponed.
missed.quote: Déjà ça n'a pas l'air évident, surtout pas quand on ne suppose pas que l'atelier soit modéré ... Là je n'ai pas la pêche pour, et laisse tomber pour le moment.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only of interest to someone reconstructing Grothendieck's 1986 combinatorial 'tame topology' programme (ateliers/maquettes). Mathematically the question resembles known quotient problems for stratified or definable spaces, so the novelty is limited.

deep.surprise_reason: A short planning page that poses a quotient problem, solves only the trivial discrete case, and drops the rest. It belongs to a little-known unpublished formalism, but contains no substantive new result or connection.
transcription_corrections: Line 1-3 likely reads: 'À supposer qu'une telle construction existe dans un cas donné, ce qui n'est pas évident, elle s'annonce un tantinet délicate.'
'Ob F, F un diagramme' appears in the image as 'Omb° F, F une figure' (Omb° possibly 'ombre ouverte').
'Supp F' — image shows 'supp F' with lower-case s, written as 'suppF'.
'(NB x ≤ y ⇒ x=y!)' — the relation symbol is a double/decorated inequality (probably ◁ or ≪ with diacritic), not plain ≤.
'Cas d'une maquette[?] A, N' — reading 'maquette' is plausible; the word may also be 'maquette' throughout line 'trouver la maquette A∖N'.
'formalisme des segments[?]' — reading uncertain; 'CF VIII p. 70 ff.' is an internal cross-reference.
